issues.description: Method getTotalNumberOfStudents: the problem statement UML declares getTotalNumberOfStudents() with return type int, the template (TODO comment) expects the same method to be implemented, but the solution implements public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object. This introduces an unexpected custom type (StudentCount) that is not in the UML or template and changes the public API students are supposed to implement, causing confusion and potential test/compile mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent with the UML and template. Prefer option A: change the solution to implement getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return an int (sum of numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents), update dependent methods (getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to use the int return value, and remove the StudentCount wrapper class from the public API. Alternatively (option B): update the problem statement UML and the template to document the StudentCount type and its API (constructor and getValue()) so students are instructed to implement/return StudentCount; however option A is recommended to match the existing UML which specifies int.

issues.description: Concept: total number of students (sum of inscribed and guest students). Problem statement / UML declares a method getTotalNumberOfStudents() with return type int. Template stub mentions implementing getTotalNumberOfStudents but provides no signature. Solution implements a method public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns a StudentCount object and exposes the numeric value via StudentCount.getValue(). The same conceptual entity (the total student count) is represented with two different types/identifiers: an int in the UML/problem and a StudentCount class + getValue() in the solution. This breaks the direct mapping students expect from the UML and may confuse students about the expected return type and how to implement or use the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution so getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns an int (the sum of numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents) and remove or stop using the StudentCount wrapper. Concretely: replace public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return new StudentCount(...); } with public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; } and update dependent methods (getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()) to use the int result. Alternatively (if a wrapper type is intentional), update the problem statement/UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and document StudentCount.getValue(). Prefer the first option to match the UML and exercise instructions.
